chunks: [Caution against obeying haughty leaders and elders:] Beware! Beware of obeying your leaders and elders!

Who felt proud of their achievements and boasted about their lineage. They hurled the (liability for) things on their Lord and quarrelled with Allah in what He did with them, contesting His decree and disputing His favours.
Certainly, they are the main foundation of obstinacy, the chief pillars of mischief and the swords of pre-Islamic boasting over forefathers.
Therefore, fear Allah, do not become antagonistic to His favours on you, nor jealous of His bounty over you

and do not obey the claimants (of Islam) whose dirty water you drink along with your clean one, whose ailments you mix with your healthiness and whose wrongs you allow to enter into your rightful matters.

key_terms.الْأَدْعِيَاءَ: Claimants (often implying false or hypocritical claimants)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the haughty leaders one should avoid obeying according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) exhorts the believers to beware of obeying haughty leaders and elders who are proud of their lineage and contest God's decree. He warns that these individuals are the foundation of tribalism and mischief, and instructs believers not to be antagonistic to God's favours or jealous of His bounty, nor to obey false claimants who mix their errors with the truth. This passage reflects the Shia critique of aristocratic arrogance (istikbar) and the corruption of religious authority by those who prioritize social status over divine justice, a theme central to the early Islamic struggle against Umayyad-style elitism.
